newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher in thin trading on Thursday ahead of the Bank of Israel's interest rate decision next week, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.08 pct to 172.57
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 162.61
Volume was a very low 89 million shekels with activity in unlinked bonds falling to only 19 million shekels.

"The market is mixed and we see different trends. Investors are divided over whether the Bank of Israel will lower its key interest rate," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities and Investments.
The Bank of Israel will announce its January monetary programme, including interest rates, on Monday after the close of trading.
"Those who believe that the interest rate will remain unchanged were buying CPI-linked bonds, but others prefer buying unlinked bonds because they forecast a moderate cut," Finn said.

Elsiha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments ascribed the run-up to institutional buyers, who are getting an influx of year-end money from investors. "The big institutional investors have more money, which they prefer to invest in bonds," he said.
Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher on low volume of seven million shekels.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
